newsitem.title: UK: MAM offers KEPIT holders to swap shares.
newsitem.headline: MAM offers KEPIT holders to swap shares.

text.p: Mercury Asset Management on Monday offered investors in Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust Plc (KEPIT) to swap their holdings for shares in Mercury European Privatisation Trust Plc (MEPT) without charges.
Investors will only have to pay the standard stamp duty of 0.5 percent, while MAM will waive the normal dealing charge of one percent on purchases and the 15 stg share exchange fee.
Under the facility, KEPIT shares and warrants will be sold in the market and the proceeds invested in MEPT shares bought in the market, MAM said.

MAM has set a deadline of October 14 for investors to apply for the swap facility. But MAM said the deadline may be changed, depending on any suspension from trading arising out of any of the proposals or offers being made to KEPIT investors.

"Our proposal is a simple share exchange facility. We consider it to be complementary to the other proposals now on offer," said Lough Callaghan, managing director of the Mercury Investment Trust Division.
Poorly performing KEPIT is subject to an offer from TR European Growth Plc which is offering shareholders in the 500 million fund 99.5 percent of asset value.
KEPIT, meanwhile, is offering shareholders the chance to redeem their investments via a Kleinwort Benson money market fund or continuing with a new Kleinwort Benson European privatisation unit trust.

MAM also announced it will be waiving dealing charges until the end of 1996 for all investors -- whether KEPIT shareholders or not -- wishing to buy MEPT shares for cash under the Mercury Investment Trust Savings Plan.
